claims.text: Treating a Pulumi Output as a plain value (for example calling toString on an Output<T>) produces placeholder text like `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` in logs, generated files, or resource properties.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ('Output value errors') exists and describes this and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
A troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
In Pulumi programs, errors can result from stringifying an Output value, branching on it, or reading it as if it were a plain value.

Pulumi Cloud returns a "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" error when another update is in progress on a stack; a page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ addresses it.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors; a page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/server-errors/ covering them.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/post-step-errors/ for post-step event failures and engine bugs.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/connection-issues/ covering network connectivity and proxy problems.

The Pulumi CLI produces `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` errors when it cannot access a self-managed (DIY) state backend, and the page /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/using-a-diy-backend/ has an anchor #error-reading-pulumimetayaml addressing it.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ about scenarios when `pulumi destroy` fails.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/interrupted-updates/ about recovering from interrupted deployments.
On Apple Silicon Macs, running x86_64 binaries under Rosetta 2 can cause crashes or hangs in Pulumi; a page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/architecture-mismatch/ addresses it.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/troubleshooting/ for resolving CI/CD pipeline issues.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/editing-state-files/ describing safe techniques for modifying Pulumi state files.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi supports `--target` and `--exclude` options to limit operations to specific resources.
Pulumi provides automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging and diagnostics, documented at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/.
Pulumi offers pre-release dev builds that can be installed to access bug fixes that haven't shipped in a stable release yet.
A guide for filing GitHub issues exists at /docs/support/filing-issues/.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
The logging guide at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/ has an #automatic-logging section.
Pulumi has a Community Slack at slack.pulumi.com that provides fast community support.
Pulumi offers paid support options.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists as the redirect target for the #conflict hash.
The logging page has a #cli-verbose-logging anchor at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the resource providing them has been created or updated.
Representing resource properties as Outputs is central to how Pulumi builds a dependency graph and runs `pulumi preview`.
The pages 'Accessing single outputs with Apply' (/docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/) and 'Working with multiple outputs' (/docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/) exist.
The Outputs section of /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/ (anchor #outputs) exists.

When an output value is concatenated, logged, or converted to a string directly rather than via `apply` or an equivalent helper, Pulumi does not raise an error by default and instead silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In Pulumi TypeScript, interpolating an Output in a template literal produces a string containing text like `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`, with no exception thrown.
In Pulumi TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an output, or letting one flow into a JSON body, produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Pulumi Python, formatting an Output in an f-string produces a string containing `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, no exception is raised, and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Pulumi Python, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
Pulumi Python provides `Output.json_dumps()` for serializing outputs to JSON.
In Pulumi Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error.
In Pulumi Go, output values are resolved inside `ApplyT`.

In Pulumi C#, interpolating an Output in a string produces text like `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`, with no exception thrown.
Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` makes Pulumi throw an exception at the point of converting an Output to a string instead of returning the placeholder text.
The `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING` environment variable is supported in TypeScript, Python, and C# (but not Go).
When an Output is converted to a string incorrectly, `pulumi up` succeeds and the placeholder text only surfaces later.
`pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` are string-composition helpers for outputs in TypeScript.
`Output.concat`, `Output.format`, and `Output.json_dumps` are string-composition helpers for outputs in Python.
`pulumi.Sprintf` and `pulumi.JSONMarshal` are string-composition helpers for outputs in Go.
`Output.Format` is a string-composition helper for outputs in C#.
The value read from an output inside an `apply` callback is only available inside that callback (or in another output derived from it).
In Pulumi TypeScript, assigning a value to an outer variable inside an `apply` callback and using it outside the callback yields `undefined` because the callback runs asynchronously later.

The `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the rest of the program's top-level code has finished running, and adding a delay does not fix this because the callback runs when the engine resolves the dependency graph.
In Pulumi TypeScript, an Output such as `bucket.bucketName` can be passed directly as the `bucket` input of `aws.s3.BucketObject` without `apply`.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values, but a handful of positions, such as a resource's logical name, cannot accept outputs.
In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on an Output evaluates the output object itself and is generally always true regardless of what the output resolves to.
In a statically typed language, branching on an `Output<bool>` is usually a compile error because an `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.

A value known when the program starts, such as a stack configuration setting read with `pulumi.Config`, an environment variable, or a hardcoded flag, is a plain value that can be branched on normally.
When a branch depends on a resource's output, the branch must move inside `apply`, with both outcomes expressed as values rather than program structure.
In Pulumi TypeScript, `vpc.vpcId.apply((id) => ...)` derives a new Output whose value depends on the branch, whereas `if (vpc.vpcId)` evaluates the Output object rather than its value.
A resource's logical name, loop bounds, and map keys must be known plain values while the program is being evaluated, before any resource exists.
Passing an Output as a resource's logical name, loop bound, or map key fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#, where these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In Pulumi Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using an Output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Pulumi Python, using an Output as a dictionary key does not raise; Python falls back to comparing and hashing the output object itself, so the lookup silently keys on the wrong thing.

When resource names or counts must depend on data known only after a resource is created, one fix is to provision dependent resources in a separate later stack that consumes the first stack's outputs through a StackReference.
The Stacks concept page has a StackReferences section (/docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences).

Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and synchronously read a resolved value out of an output; awaiting or synchronously reading an output either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output after a deployment.
A StackReference from another Pulumi program lets it consume one stack's outputs as another stack's inputs.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (for example `res.Outputs` in Go).
The Automation API concept page exists at /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
